VIII Conclusions
5G-NIDD contains a complete capture of the network traffic from a functional 5G network in the presence of different attack scenarios such as Port Scans and DoS attacks. In addition to the attack traffic, the dataset contains nonmalicious traffic from real users providing a more realistic dataset. The dataset is fully labeled specifying each flow to be malicious or benign. Moreover, each flow has a label that shows the attack type and the attacking tool used to aid multiclass classification. [...] VI-D Multi Class Classification
We also performed a multiclass classification to validate the performance in detecting the attack type. We conducted this classification for 9 different attacks called HTTP flood, ICMP flood, SYN flood, SYN scan, Slowrate DoS, TCP connect scan, UDP flood, and UDP scan along with benign traffic flows. We used the same training test split of 70:30 in this classification too. Among experiments conducted with the top most 5, 10, 15, 20, and 25 features, the experiments with the top 10 features provided greater accuracy levels with acceptable training and prediction times. Table XVI shows the average results of 10 executions of the experiment for each model. Tables XVII to XXI present the confusion matrices for each model. proposed_tests: A staged curriculum learning strategy (training on real data first, then fine-tuning with SC-CGAN synthetic samples) will yield higher macro F1 scores for minority attack classes (Slowrate DoS, UDP scan) compared to simultaneous joint training on the augmented dataset.
Introducing synthetic data too early in the training process causes mode collapse or feature drift in the CSCA-CNN model.
Grounding cost-sensitive attention mechanisms in real traffic patterns before adapting to synthetic augmentations improves detection reliability.
strengths: Directly addresses the core research goal of improving macro F1 and minority class detection on the 5G-NIDD dataset.
Proposes a specific, structured experimental design (staged curriculum vs. joint training) that is clearly testable.
Leverages the existing CSCA-CNN architecture's cost-sensitive learning component, which is theoretically aligned with handling class imbalance.
Identifies a specific failure mode (mode collapse/feature drift) that the proposed method aims to mitigate.
weaknesses: The provided sources do not contain evidence regarding the specific 'SC-CGAN' generator or its performance on this specific dataset, making the premise of its effectiveness unverified in the provided context.
The claim that early introduction of synthetic data causes 'feature drift' in this specific architecture is a theoretical assumption not supported by the provided sources.
The hypothesis relies on a complex pipeline (CSCA-CNN + SC-CGAN + Curriculum Learning) which increases the risk of implementation errors and hyperparameter sensitivity.
The provided sources are repetitive and do not offer comparative data on curriculum learning strategies for IDS.

review_comments: The hypothesis is strong in its alignment with the research goal and offers a clear, testable experimental design. It effectively targets the specific pain points of the 5G-NIDD dataset (class imbalance, minority attacks). However, the evidence quality score is moderate because the provided sources only verify the existence and structure of the CSCA-CNN and the dataset characteristics, but do not provide evidence for the specific 'SC-CGAN' component or the theoretical claim about 'feature drift' caused by early synthetic data introduction. The novelty is good as it combines curriculum learning with GAN-based augmentation in a specific IDS context, though these components exist individually in literature. The feasibility is high as all components are standard deep learning techniques.
selected_hypothesis.text: Hypothesis: A staged curriculum learning strategy that first trains the CSCA-CNN on the original imbalanced 5G-NIDD data to establish robust feature extraction, and then fine-tunes the model using SC-CGAN-generated synthetic samples for minority classes, will yield higher macro F1 scores for minority attack classes (specifically Slowrate DoS and UDP scan) compared to simultaneous joint training on the augmented dataset. This approach addresses the feasibility risk of mode collapse or feature drift caused by introducing synthetic data too early in the training process, ensuring the cost-sensitive attention mechanisms are grounded in real traffic patterns before adapting to synthetic augmentations.
selected_hypothesis.title: Staged Curriculum Learning for SC-CGAN and CSCA-CNN Integration on 5G-NIDD

evidence_sources.abstract:
VIII Conclusions
5G-NIDD contains a complete capture of the network traffic from a functional 5G network in the presence of different attack scenarios such as Port Scans and DoS attacks. In addition to the attack traffic, the dataset contains nonmalicious traffic from real users providing a more realistic dataset. The dataset is fully labeled specifying each flow to be malicious or benign. Moreover, each flow has a label that shows the attack type and the attacking tool used to aid multiclass classification. [...] VI-D Multi Class Classification
We also performed a multiclass classification to validate the performance in detecting the attack type. We conducted this classification for 9 different attacks called HTTP flood, ICMP flood, SYN flood, SYN scan, Slowrate DoS, TCP connect scan, UDP flood, and UDP scan along with benign traffic flows. We used the same training test split of 70:30 in this classification too. Among experiments conducted with the top most 5, 10, 15, 20, and 25 features, the experiments with the top 10 features provided greater accuracy levels with acceptable training and prediction times. Table XVI shows the average results of 10 executions of the experiment for each model. Tables XVII to XXI present the confusion matrices for each model. [...] The first widely known dataset for ML based intrusion detection is DARPA dataset [23, 24] which consists of simulated Denial of Service (DoS) attacks, guess password, buffer overflow, synflood, and namp attacks. Research communities developed more datasets to support ML based intrusion detection to address the we
